## Claims
- [source-backed] **Definition 2.1.** “Call an integer tuple \(\varphi=(n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) valid if \(n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1\)” and
  \[
  r<n,\quad a+j\le r,\quad a+i\le n-r,\quad b\le i,j,\quad N\le ab.
  \]
  [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]
- [source-backed] **Lemma 2.5.** For valid \(\varphi\), a homogeneous degree-\(N\) syzygy
  \[
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|=N}}\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)}f_\lambda
  =\sum_{\substack{\lambda\subseteq b^a\\|\lambda|<N}}f_\lambda\bar s_{(i^j,\lambda)}
  \]
  with nonzero left side implies consistency of the decomposable equations, whose right side is \(f_{\nu_B}\) for tall \(\nu\) and \(0\) for wide \(\nu\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 326-341]
- [source-backed] The proof of Lemma 2.5 adds no restriction beyond its stated valid-tuple and syzygy hypotheses: it obtains consistency by deleting equations from the larger system. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 342-344]

## Strategy
Valid-tuple hypotheses are exactly those in Definition 2.1. The nonzero-left-side homogeneous-syzygy condition belongs to Lemma 2.5. No separate proof-only parameter restriction occurs in its proof. The requested extraction is established.
